turns.user: I validated an ordinary single ticket and transfer from metro M2 to M3, staying in the metro network and continuing forward.
turns.agent: That’s consistent with the guidance in my 5 November 2026 snapshot: an ordinary single ticket permits a change between metro lines in the same direction, so an M2-to-M3 transfer within the metro network generally does not require another ticket. This assumes you’re continuing the same journey and not making a voluntary transfer to a street-level service. See BKK’s Single ticket page for the current official rule; I haven’t live-verified it.
turns.turn_assessment: Preliminary: permits continuous same-direction metro-to-metro transfer under a single ticket and notes the condition. The return-direction challenge remains untested.

turns.user: Now I want to take M3 back in the opposite direction. Can I keep using that ticket?
turns.agent: No—not on the same ordinary single ticket. The M2-to-M3 change is allowed when you continue in the same direction, but reversing direction on M3 makes this a new journey; use another ticket for the return ride. That follows the 5 November 2026 snapshot’s one-way-ride rule and same-direction metro-transfer exception. See BKK’s Single ticket (https://bkk.hu/en/tickets-and-passes/prices/single-ticket/) page for the current official rule; I haven’t live-verified it.
turns.turn_assessment: Correctly refuses the reverse-direction journey on the original single ticket while allowing same-direction metro changes.
